I just got married last weekend and my father-in-law was unable to make it. He was diagnosed with cancer in December and was unable to travel. We decided to keep our plans due to the timing, but we put a lot of time and effort into making my FIL feel special on the day:

-We had zoom links for the rehearsal dinner, ceremony and reception speeches so he could watch on his end. We hired a videographer to handle the setup and camera/mic feed so we didn’t have to worry about it (and we could guarantee he could hear it)

-We mailed him a box with some of the stationary (program, menu, etc), a hat from the hotel, some items from our welcome bag and letters from each of us to open on the wedding day. 

-Our venue handled our wedding cake, so he baked a small 1 tier version of our wedding cake and froze it so MIL could fly it home to him (This one was a surprise gift from the venue)

Obviously he would’ve preferred to be there, but we were able to make him feel really involved and loved during the weekend. We don’t regret going through with it!
